title: .NET program crashed
meaning: A program built with .NET closed because of an error it didn't handle. The details show the program and the error type.
steps: Update or reinstall the program.
Repair/install the required .NET version.

title: Embedded controller timeout
meaning: The laptop's embedded controller (the small chip handling battery, keyboard, fans and lid) didn't answer in time. Can cause battery or fan misreadings; usually a BIOS/firmware bug.
steps: Update the BIOS/EC firmware from the laptop maker.

title: Embedded controller unexpected data
meaning: The laptop's embedded controller sent data nobody asked for, usually because the BIOS talks to it without coordinating with Windows. Normally a firmware bug.
steps: Update the BIOS/EC firmware from the laptop maker.

title: Program crashed
meaning: A program closed unexpectedly. The details name the program and the module (DLL) where the crash happened.
steps: Update or reinstall the program.
If the module is a driver/overlay DLL, update or remove it.
Frequent crashes in many apps: test RAM.

title: Program stopped responding
meaning: A program froze and was closed (or the user closed it).
steps: Update the program.
Check for slow disk or low memory if many apps hang.

title: System popup message
meaning: Windows showed a pop-up message. Its meaning depends on the text (for example 'Delayed Write Failed' or a missing file).
steps: Read the popup text in the details.

title: Bluetooth adapter failed
meaning: The Bluetooth adapter failed and Windows stopped using it. Often after sleep; Bluetooth devices stop working.
steps: Restart the PC (full shutdown).
Update or reinstall the Bluetooth driver.
Disable power saving for the Bluetooth adapter.

title: Bluetooth connection refused
meaning: A connection attempt to a paired Bluetooth device failed or was rejected, often because the device is off or out of range. Harmless unless the device won't connect.

title: Disk has a bad block
meaning: The drive reported a bad block (a damaged area that can't be read reliably). Data on it may be lost and the drive may be failing.
steps: Back up important data now.
Check SMART status and run a surface scan on the Disk page.
Plan to replace the drive if bad blocks grow.

title: Disk controller error
meaning: Windows got an error talking to the drive. Common causes: a failing drive, a loose or bad SATA/USB cable, a bad port, or a power problem.
steps: Reseat or replace the data/power cable; try another port.
Check SMART on the Disk page.
Update the storage/chipset driver.

title: Disk not ready
meaning: A drive was not ready when Windows tried to use it. Often a USB drive or card reader that is slow to wake or was just connected.
steps: If it's an internal drive, check cables and power.
Check SMART on the Disk page.

title: Error during paging to disk
meaning: An error happened while moving memory data to or from the disk. One entry after unplugging a USB drive is harmless; repeated entries on an internal drive can mean a failing drive or cable.
steps: Check which disk is named (Harddisk0 is usually the system disk).
Check SMART and cables on the Disk page.

title: Disk predicts it will fail
meaning: The drive's own health monitoring (SMART) says it is likely to fail soon.
steps: Back up all data immediately.
Replace the drive.
Confirm SMART values on the Disk page.

title: Disk operation retried
meaning: A read/write request to the disk took too long or failed and Windows retried it. Occasional entries are tolerable; many point to a slow, failing drive, cable or controller issue.
steps: Check SMART and response times on the Disk page.
Check cables; update storage driver and SSD firmware.

title: Disk hardware error
meaning: A read/write request failed because the drive reported a hardware error. The drive is likely damaged.
steps: Back up data now.
Run SMART check and surface scan on the Disk page.
Replace the drive if errors continue.

title: Disk was removed suddenly
meaning: A drive disappeared without being safely removed. Normal if a USB drive was unplugged; on an internal drive it points to a power, cable or drive failure.
steps: If internal: check cables, power supply and SMART.
For USB: use 'Safely Remove Hardware' before unplugging.

title: Graphics driver recovered
meaning: The graphics driver stopped responding and Windows restarted it (screen may have gone black briefly). Occasional is tolerable; frequent means driver, overheating, overclock or GPU/PSU problems.
steps: Clean-install the latest (or previous stable) graphics driver.
Check GPU temperature; remove GPU overclock.
Run a GPU stress test.

title: Network cable disconnected
meaning: The Intel wired network adapter lost its link (cable unplugged, router off, or link dropped). Frequent drops point to a bad cable, port or power saving.
steps: Replace the network cable; try another router port.
Disable 'Energy Efficient Ethernet' in adapter settings.
Update the Intel network driver.

title: Network link established
meaning: The Intel wired network adapter connected; the message shows the speed (e.g. 1 Gbps full duplex). If the speed is lower than expected, check the cable.

title: Database log file error
meaning: A program's small internal database (often the browser/Web cache WebCacheV01 or Search) couldn't open a log file. Usually harmless; Windows recreates it.

title: Database feature notice
meaning: Informational message about an internal database feature being enabled. Harmless.

title: Event Log service started
meaning: The event log service started, which happens at every boot. Handy as a 'PC turned on' marker.

title: Event Log service stopped
meaning: The event log service stopped during a clean shutdown. Handy as a 'PC shut down normally' marker.

title: Previous shutdown was unexpected
meaning: The last shutdown was not clean: power loss, freeze, forced power-off or a crash. Usually appears together with Kernel-Power 41.
steps: Look for Kernel-Power 41 and BugCheck 1001 at the same time.
Check the Crash page for a blue screen.

title: Storage device was reset
meaning: The Intel RST storage driver reset a drive because a request didn't finish in time. Repeated resets cause freezes and point to a failing drive, bad cable, power-saving issues or outdated firmware/driver.
steps: Check SMART on the Disk page.
Update SSD firmware and the storage/chipset driver.
For SATA, replace the cable; try disabling link power saving.

title: Authentication error
meaning: The security system got an authentication error talking to a server (often a domain controller or network share).
steps: Check network, time sync and saved credentials.

title: Office showed a message
meaning: An Office app showed a dialog to the user (e.g. 'Do you want to save?'). The text of the dialog is in the details.

title: Crypto backup notice
meaning: Cryptographic Services couldn't back up a system file for the backup writer (often about a network driver). Known harmless message.

title: Root certificate list update failed
meaning: Windows couldn't extract an updated list of trusted root certificates, usually a temporary download or clock issue. Harmless if websites open normally.

title: No IP address from DHCP
meaning: The network adapter didn't get an address from the router/DHCP server. Common at startup or after waking; repeated means no connection.
steps: Check the cable/Wi-Fi connection and restart the router.
Run 'ipconfig /renew'.

title: IP lease denied
meaning: The router/DHCP server refused the address this PC asked for (DHCPNACK). Usually harmless when moving between networks; Windows then asks for a new address.
steps: If no connection follows, restart the router and run 'ipconfig /renew'.

title: DHCP client started
meaning: The DHCPv4 client service started (logged at boot). Normal.

title: Boot time measured
meaning: Windows recorded how long startup took (Boot Duration, in milliseconds). Useful to track slow boots.

title: App slowed down startup
meaning: A program took longer than usual to start during boot and slowed it down.
steps: Disable the named program on the Startup page if not needed.

title: Driver slowed down startup
meaning: A driver took longer than usual to initialize during boot.
steps: Update or remove the named driver.

title: Service slowed down startup
meaning: A startup service took longer than usual to start.
steps: Check or delay the named service on the Services page.

title: Shutdown time measured
meaning: Windows recorded how long shutdown took.

title: DCOM couldn't start a service
meaning: A component asked for a service that is disabled or can't start. Error 1058 means the service is disabled, often on purpose. Usually harmless.

title: Component didn't register in time
meaning: A background component was started but didn't check in within the time limit. Very common and usually harmless unless a specific app fails at the same time.

title: DCOM permission notice
meaning: A Windows component tried to use another component without the needed permission. Microsoft states this is expected and can be ignored; it doesn't affect how Windows works.

title: DCOM couldn't reach a computer
meaning: Windows couldn't talk to another computer over the network via DCOM, often a printer, server or PC that no longer exists or is offline.
steps: Remove old printers/servers that point to the named computer.
Check network/firewall if the computer should be reachable.

title: Name lookup timed out
meaning: A DNS name lookup (turning a name into an address) got no answer. For the name 'wpad' this is normal noise. Many lookups failing for real sites means a DNS or internet problem.

title: User-mode driver crashed
meaning: A driver running outside the kernel (for USB devices, sensors, phones, printers, etc.) had a problem and its host process was stopped.
steps: Find the device in the details; reconnect it.
Update or reinstall its driver.

title: Device went offline
meaning: A device using a user-mode driver went offline and was disabled after errors, often a USB device disconnecting.
steps: Reconnect the device; try another USB port or cable.
Update its driver.

title: Event log was cleared
meaning: Someone or some program cleared an event log. Normal after cleanup tools; unexpected clearing can hide problems or intrusion.
steps: Check which user did it (details) and whether it was intended.

title: Security log was cleared
meaning: The Security audit log was cleared. Normal if done by an admin; otherwise it can hide traces of an intrusion.
steps: Confirm with the user/admin that the clearing was intended.

title: Can't find domain controller
meaning: Group Policy couldn't get the name of a domain controller, usually a network or DNS problem on a domain PC.
steps: Check the network and that DNS points to the domain's DNS servers.

title: Can't resolve computer name
meaning: Group Policy couldn't resolve the computer name, usually a DNS or domain membership problem.
steps: Check DNS settings; run 'gpupdate /force'.

title: Can't read policy files
meaning: Group Policy couldn't read policy files from the domain controller (gpt.ini). Network, DNS or permission problem.
steps: Check network access to the domain; run 'gpupdate /force'.

title: Policy settings not applied
meaning: Windows failed to apply one group of policy settings (named in the message).
steps: Run 'gpresult /h report.html' to see the error.

title: No network for Group Policy
meaning: Group Policy failed because there was no network connection to a domain controller. Common at startup on Wi-Fi or VPN; a problem if it repeats.
steps: Check network connection; run 'gpupdate /force' once connected.

title: Policy script failed
meaning: A startup, shutdown, logon or logoff script from Group Policy failed to run.
steps: Check the script path and permissions in the details.

title: Hypervisor didn't start
meaning: Hyper-V (virtualization) couldn't start because hardware virtualization (Intel VT-x / AMD-V) is off in the BIOS or not available.
steps: Enable virtualization (VT-x/AMD-V/SVM) in the BIOS if Hyper-V, WSL or VBS is needed.

title: Last shutdown/boot status
meaning: Records whether the previous shutdown and boot completed. If either status is 'false', the previous session ended badly; look for Kernel-Power 41 nearby.

title: Boot type
meaning: Records the startup type: 0x0 is a full (cold) boot, 0x1 is a Fast Startup resume, 0x2 is resume from hibernation.

title: Trace session stopped
meaning: An internal diagnostic tracing session stopped with an error, typically 'ReadyBoot' with 0xC0000188 (log full). Harmless.

title: System time changed
meaning: The clock was changed, usually by time synchronization or on resume. Large or frequent jumps can point to a weak CMOS battery.

title: Windows started
meaning: The operating system started. Marks the beginning of each boot.

title: Windows shut down
meaning: The operating system is shutting down. Its absence before a 12 means the last shutdown was not clean.

title: Driver failed to load for device
meaning: A driver didn't load for a device during startup. Very often harmless (e.g. WudfRd for a device that loads later); investigate if a device isn't working.
steps: Check Device Manager / Drivers page for devices with errors.
Reinstall or update the driver for the named device.

title: App blocked device removal
meaning: A program was using a device (usually a USB drive) and stopped it from being ejected. The details name the program.

title: Device had a problem starting
meaning: A device failed to start. The details include the device and a problem code (the same as the Device Manager error code).
steps: Check the device on the Drivers page.
Reinstall or update its driver; for USB try another port.

title: Unexpected restart
meaning: The PC restarted without shutting down properly first: power was lost, the system froze and was reset, or it crashed. If BugcheckCode in the details is not 0, there was a blue screen; if it is 0, power was cut or the PC was hard-reset.
steps: Check the Crash page for a blue screen at the same time.
If BugcheckCode is 0: check PSU, power cable, overheating, or a held power button.
Run a stress test to see if the PC shuts off under load.

title: Entering sleep
meaning: Windows is going to sleep or hibernation. The details show why (button, lid, idle timer, or an app request).

title: Shutdown: critical temperature
meaning: Windows turned the PC off because a temperature sensor (thermal zone) reported a critical level. This protects the hardware from heat damage.
steps: Check CPU/GPU temperatures under load.
Clean dust from fans and heatsinks; check that all fans spin.
Renew thermal paste if temperatures stay high.

title: Resumed from sleep
meaning: The system woke up from sleep or hibernation. Normal.

title: Shutdown started
meaning: The kernel power manager started a shutdown or restart. Logged on every normal shutdown.

title: Firmware changed CPU settings on resume
meaning: The BIOS/UEFI changed some processor memory settings (MTRRs) while the PC was hibernating. Harmless if the PC wakes up and runs normally.

title: App requested sleep/shutdown
meaning: A program asked Windows to change the power state (sleep, hibernate or shut down) through a system function. The details name the program.

title: Entering Modern Standby
meaning: The device is entering Modern Standby (screen-off, low-power mode on newer laptops and tablets). Normal.

title: Exiting Modern Standby
meaning: The device woke from Modern Standby. The details show how long it slept and what woke it.

title: CPU speed limited by firmware
meaning: The BIOS/firmware is holding a processor below its normal speed, usually because of heat, a weak power supply/charger, or a power-saving setting. Occasional entries are common on laptops.
steps: Check CPU temperature and throttling on the Stress page.
On laptops, test with the original charger plugged in.
Update the BIOS if it repeats while cool.

title: Memory test: no errors
meaning: Windows Memory Diagnostic finished and found no errors.

title: Memory test found errors
meaning: Windows Memory Diagnostic detected hardware errors in RAM.
steps: Test modules one at a time to find the bad stick.
Replace the faulty module.

title: Memory test: no errors
meaning: Windows Memory Diagnostic finished and found no errors (logged after the next sign-in).

title: Memory test found errors
meaning: Windows Memory Diagnostic detected hardware errors in RAM (logged after the next sign-in).
steps: Test modules one at a time to find the bad stick.
Replace the faulty module.

title: Delayed write failed
meaning: Windows couldn't finish saving data to a drive, so some data may be lost. Typical with a USB drive unplugged too early, or a failing drive/cable.
steps: Run chkdsk on the drive named in the message.
Check SMART and cables on the Disk page.

title: File system is corrupted
meaning: The file system structure on a drive is damaged and can't be used safely. Caused by power loss, forced shutdowns, or a failing disk.
steps: Run 'chkdsk X: /f' on the named drive (restart may be needed).
Check SMART on the Disk page.
Back up important data.

title: Volume health check
meaning: Windows checked a drive's file system. If the message says the volume is healthy, nothing is needed. If it says it needs an offline scan/repair (chkdsk), the file system has errors.
steps: If repair is needed: run 'chkdsk X: /f' and restart.
Check SMART if it keeps coming back.

title: Transaction manager error
meaning: The part of NTFS that tracks transactions on a volume hit an error it can't retry. Often related to file system damage or removable drives.
steps: Run 'chkdsk X: /f' on the named volume.
Run 'sfc /scannow' if it's the system drive.

title: Failed to flush transaction log
meaning: Windows couldn't write file system bookkeeping to a volume; data corruption may follow. Very common with USB drives removed early or disks going to sleep.
steps: Identify the volume (HarddiskVolumeN) in the details.
Run chkdsk on it; check SMART on the Disk page.

title: Woke from sleep
meaning: The PC returned from sleep. 'Wake Source' shows what woke it (power button, mouse, network adapter, timer).

title: Low memory detected
meaning: Windows diagnosed a low virtual memory condition. The details list the programs using the most memory.
steps: Close or fix the program using the most memory.
Make sure the page file is enabled.
Consider adding RAM.

title: Restart Manager session started
meaning: An installer started a session to close/restart apps using files it needs to update. Normal during installs.

title: Restart Manager session ended
meaning: The installer's Restart Manager session ended. Normal.

title: Search can't reach location
meaning: Windows Search couldn't access one of its indexed locations (often Offline Files or a disconnected drive). Harmless.

title: Successful sign-in
meaning: An account signed in successfully (includes system and network sign-ins).

title: Failed sign-in
meaning: A sign-in attempt failed (wrong password or unknown user). Many in a short time can mean password guessing or a saved wrong password.
steps: Check the account name and source address in the details.

title: User account created
meaning: A new user account was created. Check it was intended.
steps: Confirm the new account is known to the owner.

title: Account locked out
meaning: An account was locked after too many failed sign-ins.
steps: Find the device using an old password (details show the source).

title: Kerberos: wrong server identity
meaning: A domain sign-in ticket was rejected by a server (KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED). Usually duplicate or stale DNS records or computer names on a domain network.
steps: Check DNS records for the named server.
Rejoin the computer to the domain if its account is broken.

title: License acquisition failed
meaning: Windows couldn't obtain a license from Microsoft's servers, usually because the network wasn't ready. Harmless if Windows shows as activated.

title: Activation failed
meaning: Windows activation failed. The hr= code shows why (no internet, invalid key, or activation server unreachable).
steps: Check activation status in Settings > System > Activation.

title: License service rescheduled
meaning: The Software Protection service scheduled itself to restart later. Normal.

title: Package change finished
meaning: An update package changed state (e.g. Installed). The result code shows success or failure.

title: Restart needed for package
meaning: A restart is required before an update package can finish installing.

title: Clock not synced for a long time
meaning: The clock hasn't been synchronized for a long time (often 24 hours) because no time source answered. The clock may drift.
steps: Check internet access.
Run 'w32tm /resync' as administrator.

title: No reply from time server
meaning: The configured time server didn't answer after several tries. Harmless when offline; repeated with internet may mean a firewall blocks time (UDP port 123).
steps: Check that the clock is correct.
Try another time server in Date & Time settings.

title: No domain time source found
meaning: The PC tried to find a domain controller for time and couldn't. Normal on home PCs not in a domain, and at startup before the network is up.

title: Time server name not resolved
meaning: The time server name (e.g. time.windows.com) couldn't be looked up, usually because the network wasn't ready yet. Harmless if the clock is correct.

title: VM time provider not used
meaning: The virtual-machine time provider says it isn't needed because this isn't a virtual machine. Normal on physical PCs.

title: Firmware rejected Secure Boot update
meaning: The BIOS/UEFI returned an error while Windows tried to update Secure Boot certificates.
steps: Update the BIOS/UEFI from the PC maker.

title: Secure Boot update error
meaning: An unexpected error happened while updating Secure Boot data; Windows retries at the next restart. Also logged when Secure Boot is disabled.
steps: Restart and check if the event returns.
Update the BIOS; check Secure Boot is enabled.

title: Secure Boot certs not yet applied
meaning: New Secure Boot certificates are ready but haven't been written to the firmware yet. Part of Microsoft's certificate rollout (old 2011 certificates expire in 2026).
steps: Install Windows updates and a current BIOS; restart.

title: Secure Boot certificates updated
meaning: This device has installed the updated Secure Boot certificates/keys. Good.

title: Signed in with temporary profile
meaning: Windows couldn't load the user's profile and signed in with a temporary one. Files and settings seem missing and changes will be lost at sign-out.
steps: Don't save work in the temporary profile.
Fix the profile's registry entry (ProfileList) or restore from backup.
Check disk health.

title: Profile file still in use
meaning: At sign-out, some program still held the user's registry file; Windows unloaded it anyway. Normal and harmless.

title: Driver installed for device
meaning: Windows finished installing a driver for a device. Status 0x0 means success; any other status means the install failed.

title: Blue screen (crash) occurred
meaning: The PC restarted after a blue screen (bugcheck). The message shows the stop code and where a crash dump was saved.
steps: Open the Crash page to see the stop code and the likely driver.
Update or roll back the driver named in the dump.
Test RAM and disk if crashes have different codes.

title: Fatal hardware error recorded
meaning: After a restart, Windows logged a fatal hardware error saved from the previous crash. The details name the component (processor, memory, PCI Express).
steps: Note the component and error source in the details.
Remove overclocks/undervolts and load BIOS defaults.
Test RAM and run a CPU stress test.

title: Corrected PCI Express error
meaning: A PCI Express link (to GPU, NVMe SSD, network card, etc.) had an error that was fixed automatically. Often harmless noise caused by power saving (ASPM); many per minute can slow the system.
steps: Note the device ID in the details to find which card it is.
Update BIOS and chipset drivers.
Reseat the card or try another slot.

title: Fatal CPU/hardware error
meaning: The processor reported an uncorrectable hardware error (machine check), which crashes the system. Common causes: unstable overclock/undervolt, overheating, bad CPU, RAM or motherboard.
steps: Load BIOS defaults and remove any overclock or undervolt.
Check temperatures and run a stress test.
Update the BIOS; test RAM.

title: Corrected CPU error
meaning: The processor detected and fixed an internal error (cache or bus). A few are harmless; frequent ones suggest an unstable overclock/undervolt, heat, or hardware starting to fail.
steps: Remove overclock/undervolt and load BIOS defaults.
Update the BIOS; run a CPU stress test.

title: Memory hardware error
meaning: A memory error was reported through the processor's error reporting (machine check). Usually faulty or unstable RAM, or wrong RAM timings/XMP/EXPO settings.
steps: Disable XMP/EXPO and test with default RAM speed.
Run a RAM test; test one module at a time.

title: Corrected memory error
meaning: A memory error was detected and fixed. Occasional ones may be tolerated; repeated ones point to failing or unstable RAM (often too-aggressive XMP/EXPO settings).
steps: Run a RAM test.
Try default RAM settings (disable XMP/EXPO).

title: Malware detected
meaning: Microsoft Defender found malware or unwanted software. The details show the threat name and file path.
steps: Check that event 1117 (action taken) follows.
Run a full scan; review the file path.

title: Malware action taken
meaning: Microsoft Defender took action on a threat (quarantined, removed or allowed).
steps: Review Protection history to confirm the threat is resolved.

title: Malware action failed
meaning: Microsoft Defender tried to remove a threat but failed (non-critical failure). The threat may still be present.
steps: Run a full scan or a Microsoft Defender Offline scan.

title: Malware action critical fail
meaning: Microsoft Defender hit a critical error while acting on a threat. The threat is likely still present.
steps: Run a Microsoft Defender Offline scan.
Consider a second-opinion scanner.

title: Definition update failed
meaning: Microsoft Defender couldn't update its security intelligence (virus definitions). Protection gets outdated if it keeps failing.
steps: Check internet access; update Defender manually from Windows Security.

title: New definitions failed to load
meaning: New security intelligence couldn't be loaded, so Defender went back to the previous version.
steps: Update Defender manually; restart the PC.

title: Real-time protection error
meaning: A part of real-time protection hit an error and stopped.
steps: Restart the PC; update Defender.
Check for conflicting antivirus software.

title: Real-time protection off
meaning: Real-time protection was turned off. Normal if another antivirus is installed; otherwise the PC is less protected.
steps: Turn it back on in Windows Security unless another antivirus is active.

title: Defender settings changed
meaning: A Microsoft Defender setting changed. Very frequent and normal (updates change settings); unexpected exclusions added can be a sign of malware.

title: Antivirus engine stopped
meaning: The Microsoft Defender engine stopped because of an unexpected error.
steps: Update Defender and restart; check for conflicting antivirus.

title: Update installed
meaning: Windows Update installed an update successfully.

title: Update failed to install
meaning: An update failed to install. The error code (0x8...) tells why. Windows usually retries later.
steps: Note the KB number and error code.
Run Windows Update troubleshooter; free disk space.
Run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' then 'sfc /scannow'.

title: Update check failed
meaning: Windows Update couldn't check for updates. Usually network or proxy problems.
steps: Check internet/proxy settings; retry later.

title: Update download failed
meaning: Windows Update failed to download an update. Often network issues, a proxy, or a damaged update cache.
steps: Check internet connection and free space.
Reset the update cache (SoftwareDistribution folder).

title: Update install started
meaning: Windows Update started installing an update.

title: Update download started
meaning: Windows Update started downloading an update.

title: Sign-in step is slow
meaning: A sign-in component (often Group Policy) is taking a long time. Repeated entries explain slow sign-ins.
steps: See event 6006 for how long it took.
Check network and startup programs.

title: Sign-in step took long
meaning: A sign-in component (often Group Policy) took a long time to finish. The details show how many seconds.
steps: Check network/domain connectivity if it's GPClient.

title: User signed in
meaning: A user signed in to Windows. Useful to see when the PC was used.

title: User signed out
meaning: A user signed out of Windows.

title: Wi-Fi limited, auto-recovery
meaning: Windows detected limited Wi-Fi connectivity and tried to recover by resetting the adapter.
steps: Update the Wi-Fi driver.
Disable power saving for the Wi-Fi adapter.
Check router signal and channel.

title: Wi-Fi connected
meaning: The PC connected to a wireless network. Details show the network name and security type.

title: Wi-Fi connection failed
meaning: Connecting to a wireless network failed. The details give the reason (wrong password, weak signal, network not found).
steps: Check the reason in the details.
Forget the network and reconnect.

title: Wi-Fi disconnected
meaning: The PC disconnected from a wireless network. Normal when leaving or sleeping; many unexpected disconnects point to signal or driver issues.

title: Wi-Fi vendor module stopped
meaning: A Wi-Fi add-on module from the adapter vendor stopped. Often linked to Wi-Fi driver problems.
steps: Update or reinstall the Wi-Fi driver.

title: Wi-Fi security failed
meaning: The wireless security step (password/authentication) failed while connecting.
steps: Re-enter the Wi-Fi password.
Update the Wi-Fi driver; check router security mode.

title: WMI event filter not reactivated
meaning: A WMI event filter (a query left by software such as old OEM tools) couldn't be reactivated. Usually harmless.

title: WMI query error
meaning: A program's WMI query (system information request) returned an error. Very frequent and normally harmless.

title: Program installed
meaning: Windows Installer installed a product. 'Success or error status: 0' means success; any other number is an error code.

title: Program removed
meaning: Windows Installer removed a product. Status 0 means success.

title: Installation completed
meaning: A product was installed successfully by Windows Installer.

title: Installation failed
meaning: A Windows Installer setup failed. Look at events just before it (often 11xxx with an error number) for the reason.
steps: Run the installer again as administrator.
Check free disk space; remove old versions first.

title: Program removal completed
meaning: A product was removed successfully by Windows Installer.

title: Netlogon not needed
meaning: This PC is in a workgroup, not a domain, so the Netlogon service isn't needed. Harmless.

title: No domain controller at startup
meaning: The PC couldn't set up a secure session with a domain controller. Common at boot before the network is ready. If it repeats later on a domain PC, sign-in and policies may fail.

title: NVIDIA graphics exception
meaning: The NVIDIA driver reported a GPU error ('Graphics Exception', also called an Xid error). Often from an unstable overclock, bad driver, overheating or a failing GPU.
steps: Clean-install the NVIDIA driver.
Remove GPU overclock; check temps under load.

title: NVIDIA GPU error
meaning: The NVIDIA driver logged a GPU error with codes for NVIDIA's own diagnostics. Repeated entries point to driver, power or GPU hardware problems.
steps: Clean-install the NVIDIA driver.
Check GPU power cables and PSU; run a GPU stress test.

title: NVIDIA GPU error occurred
meaning: The NVIDIA driver reported an error on the GPU ('Error occurred on GPUID'), often together with a driver reset (Display 4101) or a crash.
steps: Clean-install the NVIDIA driver.
Remove overclock; check temps and power cables.

title: Duplicate disk signature
meaning: Two disks have the same identity (signature), usually after cloning a drive. Windows takes one of them offline.
steps: Bring the disk online in Disk Management (this gives it a new signature).

title: Performance counter didn't open
meaning: A performance counter provider (e.g. for BITS or a service) failed to open. Harmless for normal use; only monitoring tools are affected.

title: Performance counter DLL not loaded
meaning: Windows couldn't load a performance counter library. Harmless for normal use; can be fixed with 'lodctr /r' if monitoring tools need it.

title: TLS credential error
meaning: Windows couldn't create credentials for a secure (TLS) connection. Common and often harmless; matters only if a specific app can't connect securely.

title: No shared TLS cipher
meaning: A client tried a secure connection but none of its encryption methods are allowed on this PC. Usually an old client; harmless on home PCs.

title: TLS alert received
meaning: The other side of a secure connection sent an error and closed it. Very common background noise from apps and websites.

title: TLS alert sent
meaning: This PC sent an error on a secure connection and closed it. Common background noise.

title: Service failed to start
meaning: A Windows or app service couldn't start. The message gives the service name and reason. Often left over from uninstalled software or a missing driver.
steps: Check the service on the Services page.
If it belongs to removed software, set it to Disabled.
Reinstall the app/driver it belongs to.

title: Service dependency failed
meaning: A service didn't start because another service it needs failed first. Fix the first service and this one follows.
steps: Find the earlier 7000/7009/7023 event for the service it depends on.

title: Service start timed out
meaning: A service took too long (usually over 30 seconds) to start. Common on slow disks or busy startups; usually followed by 7000.
steps: Check disk health and startup load.
Update or remove the software owning the service.

title: Service didn't respond in time
meaning: A service didn't respond to a request within the time limit (usually 30 seconds). Occasional is common; repeats suggest a hanging service or slow disk.
steps: Check which service it is; update or disable it if not needed.
Check disk health.

title: Service hung on starting
meaning: A service started but got stuck and never finished starting.
steps: Restart the PC; if it repeats, update or reinstall the owning software.

title: Service stopped with error
meaning: A service ended with an error code. The message explains the error.
steps: Look up the named service on the Services page.
Reinstall or update the software it belongs to.

title: Service stopped with its own error
meaning: A service ended with an error specific to that service. Meaning depends on the service.
steps: Check the service and its app's own logs.
Reinstall/update the software it belongs to.

title: Boot driver(s) failed to load
meaning: One or more drivers set to load at startup did not load. Often leftover drivers from removed software or unused hardware.
steps: Check the listed driver names on the Drivers page.
Remove leftovers of uninstalled software (VPN, antivirus, tools).

title: Service crashed (recovery set)
meaning: A service stopped unexpectedly; Windows will take the recovery action set for it (often restart). Repeats mean the service or its app is unstable.
steps: Check Application Error 1000 at the same time for the crashing program.
Update or reinstall the owning software.

title: Service recovery action failed
meaning: Windows tried to recover a crashed service (e.g. restart it) and that failed too.
steps: Check the service on the Services page and restart it manually.
Reinstall the software it belongs to.

title: Service crashed
meaning: A service stopped unexpectedly. The message shows how many times this happened.
steps: Check Application Error 1000 at the same time for details.
Update or reinstall the owning software.

title: Service started/stopped
meaning: A service changed state (running or stopped). Logged constantly; normal.

title: Service couldn't log on
meaning: A service set to run under a specific user account couldn't log on, usually because that account's password changed.
steps: Update the password in the service's Log On settings.

title: Service start type changed
meaning: A service's startup type was changed (e.g. Automatic to Manual). Windows Update and BITS do this routinely.

title: Service slow to shut down
meaning: A service didn't shut down properly after being told the PC was shutting down. Can make shutdown slow.
steps: Update the software owning the service.

title: New service installed
meaning: A new service or driver was installed. Normal when installing software; unknown services can indicate malware.
steps: Check the service name and file path are from known software.

title: Missing program component
meaning: A program couldn't start because a required component (usually a Visual C++ runtime) is missing.
steps: Install/repair the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables (x86 and x64).
Reinstall the program.

title: Program component setup failed
meaning: Windows couldn't prepare the components a program needs (its manifest or a referenced runtime is missing or broken). Usually paired with event 33.
steps: Install/repair Visual C++ Redistributables.
Reinstall the program.

title: Storage device was reset
meaning: The SATA (AHCI) storage driver reset a drive because a request didn't finish in time. Repeated resets cause freezes and point to a failing drive, bad cable, power-saving issues or outdated firmware/driver.
steps: Check SMART on the Disk page.
Update SSD firmware and the storage/chipset driver.
For SATA, replace the cable; try disabling link power saving.

title: NVMe controller error
meaning: The NVMe SSD's controller reported an error. Often a failing SSD, outdated SSD firmware, or overheating.
steps: Check SMART and temperature on the Disk page.
Update the SSD firmware from the manufacturer.
Back up data if errors repeat.

title: Storage device was reset
meaning: The NVMe storage driver reset a drive because a request didn't finish in time. Repeated resets cause freezes and point to a failing drive, bad cable, power-saving issues or outdated firmware/driver.
steps: Check SMART on the Disk page.
Update SSD firmware and the storage/chipset driver.
For SATA, replace the cable; try disabling link power saving.

title: IP address conflict
meaning: Another device on the network is using the same IP address as this PC. Internet or network access will be unreliable.
steps: Set the adapter to obtain an IP automatically (DHCP).
Restart the router; fix any duplicate static IPs.

title: Connection reused too quickly
meaning: Windows couldn't open a new network connection because the same local/remote port pair was used very recently. Occasional is fine; frequent means an app opens huge numbers of connections.
steps: Find the program making many connections (Network page).

title: Out of network ports
meaning: Windows ran out of temporary network ports, so new connections fail. Usually one program leaks connections.
steps: Find the program with the most connections (e.g. 'netstat -ano').
Restart or update that program.

title: Planned restart/shutdown
meaning: A user or program started a restart or shutdown. The details show who/what did it and why (e.g. Windows Update).

title: Crash dump driver failed to load
meaning: Windows couldn't load the driver that writes crash dump files. If a blue screen happens, no dump may be saved.
steps: Check pagefile and crash dump settings (System > Advanced > Startup and Recovery).

title: Crash dump setup failed
meaning: Windows couldn't prepare to save crash dump files at boot. Harmless by itself (common when the page file is off or small), but blue screens won't leave a dump.
steps: Enable a system-managed page file on C:.
Set 'Automatic memory dump' in Startup and Recovery.

title: Page file too small for dumps
meaning: The page file couldn't be configured for crash dumps, usually because it's disabled or too small. Crash dumps won't be saved.
steps: Enable a system-managed page file on the system drive.

title: Crash dump creation failed
meaning: A blue screen happened but the crash dump file couldn't be written, often due to a small page file, low disk space, or a disk problem.
steps: Free space on C: and enable a system-managed page file.
Check the disk on the Disk page.

title: Restore points deleted (space)
meaning: Shadow copies (restore points) on a volume were deleted because their storage couldn't grow in time.
steps: Free disk space or increase System Protection space.

title: Oldest restore point deleted
meaning: The oldest shadow copy (restore point) was deleted to stay under the space limit. Normal.

title: Shadow copies aborted (limit)
meaning: Shadow copies were aborted because their storage hit the size limit.
steps: Increase System Protection space or free disk space.

title: Shadow copy component unavailable
meaning: A Volume Shadow Copy component couldn't be started. Very common and usually harmless unless backups or restore points fail.

title: Shadow copy error
meaning: The Volume Shadow Copy service (used by backups and restore points) hit an unexpected error.
steps: Check that backups/System Restore work.
Restart the 'Volume Shadow Copy' service.

title: Shadow copy access denied
meaning: The Volume Shadow Copy service got 'access denied' talking to a component. Often harmless; can break some backup software.
steps: Check that backups complete successfully.

title: Shadow copy device error
meaning: The Volume Shadow Copy service got an error from a drive. Can affect backups and restore points; sometimes caused by drives without enough free space.
steps: Check the named drive on the Disk page.
Free space on the drive.

title: Shadow copy writer problem
meaning: The Volume Shadow Copy service found an inconsistency while contacting backup helpers (writers).
steps: Run 'vssadmin list writers' to find failed writers.
Restart the PC and retry the backup.

title: Problem report created
meaning: Windows recorded a problem report. 'Event Name' shows the type: APPCRASH (app crash), AppHangB1 (app froze), BlueScreen, or LiveKernelEvent (driver/hardware hiccup, often graphics).
steps: Read 'Event Name' and the program name in the details.
LiveKernelEvent 141/117: check the graphics driver and GPU.

title: Check Disk results at boot
meaning: Shows the result of a disk check (chkdsk) that ran during startup. Read the text: 'no problems found' is fine; repaired or bad sectors deserve a closer look.
steps: Read the report for 'bad sectors' or repaired files.
Check SMART on the Disk page.
